summary: When Apache Shiro is used with the Jakarta EE integration module, the automatic form saving...
description:
When Apache Shiro is used with the Jakarta EE integration module, the automatic form saving feature weakens the security of a form that is resubmitted after login.
Cookies set by the application during the resubmission could lose their security attributes, such as `Secure` and `SameSite`.
In addition, the resubmitted form data and cookies could be sent to an untrusted host.
This issue affects Apache Shiro from 2.0.0-alpha through 3.0.1, only when using `shiro-jakarta-ee` integration module with form saving enabled (the default).

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which no longer replays the form over the network, and avoids this class of issues entirely.
Alternatively, you can set the `org.apache.shiro.form-resubmit-host` (String) and `org.apache.shiro.form-resubmit-port` (Integer) system properties to restrict the host and port that Shiro will connect to when resubmitting a form.

summary: Authorization annotations, such as @RequiresRoles and @RequiresPermissions, are not always...
description:
Authorization annotations, such as @RequiresRoles and @RequiresPermissions, are not always enforced in some class or interface hierarchies.
Annotations declared on an interface were not enforced when using the shiro-guice, shiro-aspectj, shiro-cdi or shiro-jakarta-ee modules.
In addition, annotations declared on a class or a superclass were not always enforced when using shiro-guice or shiro-aspectj, allowing an unauthorized caller to invoke methods that should be protected.
This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.1, with impact depending on module and where annotations are declared.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which fixes the issue. The annotation closest to the invoked method now takes precedence.
Alternatively, declare authorization annotations directly on each protected implementing method.

summary: Kunai, a security monitoring tool, contains a time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race...
description:
Kunai, a security monitoring tool, contains a time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in its mount namespace (mnt ns) caching logic. When resolving a security event that references a specific process PID and an expected mount namespace, the Switcher::new function read /proc/<pid>/ns/mnt to determine the target namespace and cached the result under the expected namespace key without verifying that the resolved namespace actually matched the expected one.

An attacker with local access could exploit this by either (1) arranging for the referenced PID to be reused by a process in a different namespace (e.g., the host namespace) before Kunai resolves it, or (2) calling unshare or setns on the target process after the event is generated but before the namespace is resolved. In either case, the wrong namespace (potentially the host's own namespace) would be cached under the container's namespace key.

The security impact is that subsequent container security events would be resolved against host filesystem paths rather than container paths. This undermines the integrity of the security monitoring data: container activity could be misattributed to the host, host activity could be misattributed to a container, and file-path-based detections or alerts would reference incorrect paths. An attacker could potentially use this to obscure malicious activity within a container by making it appear as benign host activity, or to generate misleading security alerts.

The vulnerability requires local access to the system and a specific timing window between event generation and namespace resolution. No remote attack vector or user interaction is required.

This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.1, only when accounts with an empty stored credential exist.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which fixes the issue.
Alternatively, avoid storing empty credentials, and reject empty passwords in the application.

This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.1, only when the principal tag is used.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which escapes the output.
Alternatively, validate principal values on input.

summary: Apache Shiro is vulnerable to session fixation when a user is authenticated via the "Remember me"...
description:
Apache Shiro is vulnerable to session fixation when a user is authenticated via the "Remember me" functionality. In affected versions, when a subject is restored from a "Remember me" cookie, the existing session is not invalidated, nor is a new session created with a new ID.
Additionally, session IDs were accepted from the request URL even when session ID URL rewriting was disabled.
This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.0, only when RememberMe functionality is enabled.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.1 or later, which fixes the issue by invalidating the existing session and creating a new session with a new ID when a subject is restored from a "Remember me" cookie, and by ignoring session IDs in the URL when URL rewriting is disabled.

summary: visualTicket is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) across multiple endpoints. State...

A remote attacker can persuade an authenticated user (including administrator) into navigating to a prepared URL, causing the victim's browser to issue requests that carry the active session cookie and perform unintended actions.




This issue was partially addressed in version 20260817: settings changes and bulk refunds require POST with a CSRF token, and the session cookie is set with SameSite=Lax, which limits cross-site requests.

summary: visualTicket is vulnerable to information exposure through JSONP on session-bound cart service...
description:
visualTicket is vulnerable to information exposure through JSONP on session-bound cart service endpoints. Session-bound data (including the session id, cart id, item ids, ticket/event metadata, quantities and prices) is returned inside a script wrapper, and since the symfony session token can also be passed in the URL, a remote attacker who obtains the token can read the cart session token and cart data.




This issue was mitigated in version 20260817: the session cookie is set with SameSite=Lax, which prevents other websites from reading cart data of the victim’s session.

summary: visualTicket is vulnerable to information exposure through an error message in the order creation...

This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

summary: visualTicket is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference  in the cart service. The server...
description:
visualTicket is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference  in the cart service. The server modifies or deletes a cart item based solely on the supplied "cart_id" without checking whether the object belongs to the current symfony session. Cart identifiers are created sequentially and allows prediction of valid values. An attacker holding an independent session can reference another user's "cart_id" and change its state, for example altering the quantity or deleting the item.  This allows modification or deletion of items in another user's cart, alteration of the cart total, and disruption of the reservation/purchase process.




This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

summary: An uncontrolled search path vulnerability (CWE-427) in statically linked OpenSSL libraries within...
description: An uncontrolled search path vulnerability (CWE-427) in statically linked OpenSSL libraries within Netskope Client (stAgentSvc.exe) and Endpoint DLP (epdlp.exe) on Windows allows an authenticated local attacker to execute arbitrary code with elevated SYSTEM privileges. The services retain internal build-time paths referencing a secondary drive location. On Windows systems where default volume permissions allow standard users to create root-level directories on secondary drives, an attacker can place a malicious configuration file (openssl.cnf) that is loaded under the NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM context upon service startup or system reboot. Under default operating system permissions, macOS and Linux are not susceptible, and mobile platforms are unaffected.

summary: The httpx Ruby gem parses JSON response bodies through its transcoder layer. HTTPX::Response#json...
description: The httpx Ruby gem parses JSON response bodies through its transcoder layer. HTTPX::Response#json delegates to Transcoder::JSON.decode, and when the oj gem is loaded and multi_json is absent, the decoder falls back to json_load, which calls Oj.load(response.to_s) with no mode option. Oj.load defaults to :object mode, in which a response document can allocate any already-loaded Ruby class ("^o":"ClassName") and set its instance variables, or resolve a class or module reference ("^c":"Name"). An attacker who controls, or can influence, the URL an application fetches with HTTPX.get(url).json therefore controls object instantiation in the victim process. With a matching gadget chain, this issue can potentially cause remote code execution. Affects httpx 1.9.0; fixed in 1.9.1.
